description.t: ALIGNED TEST VERSION: This teaching draft demonstrates constructive alignment for Differential Calculus. Students analyze engineering functions, limits and continuity; calculate and verify derivatives; and construct related-rates and optimization models. They explain their mathematical reasoning and communicate engineering recommendations with honest limitations and consideration for workers and communities. Weekly practice and assessment use the same mathematical objectives. Program Outcomes labeled TEST ONLY are provisional examples, not official institutional references. This draft must not be submitted as an officially verified syllabus.

clos.title: Functions, limits and continuity
clos.statement: Analyze engineering functions, graphs, limits and continuity, explaining domains, units and the assumptions used in mathematical reasoning.

clos.title: Differentiation and verification
clos.statement: Compute derivatives of algebraic, trigonometric, exponential, logarithmic and implicit functions, verify solution steps and interpret rates of change in engineering problems.

clos.title: Engineering calculus models
clos.statement: Construct and analyze related-rates, curve-analysis and optimization models for industrial engineering decisions, justify mathematical assumptions and explain effects on workers and communities.

clos.title: Responsible mathematical communication
clos.statement: Evaluate and communicate a calculus-based engineering recommendation with verified calculations, clear assumptions, honest limitations and an explanation of its effects on workers and communities.

ilos.text: Represent an engineering quantity as a function and identify its domain and units.

plan.activities: Work through functions and engineering quantities using an engineering example. Represent an engineering quantity as a function and identify its domain and units. Compare mathematical reasoning in pairs, check units and assumptions, and explain any disagreement.
plan.tasks: Individual worked engineering problem and short oral explanation: Represent an engineering quantity as a function and identify its domain and units. Submit calculations or graphs, justify each step and verify the result against an independent calculation or graphical check.
plan.values: Community-orientedness: during the functions and engineering quantities activity, identify who could be affected by an incorrect engineering calculation, peer-check the assumptions and explain how accurate, honest results protect workers and communities.
